input.stem: An alkaline aqueous mixture containing sodium hydroxide and sodium carbonate is titrated at 298 K. The titration up to the phenolphthalein end point requires the complete addition of a standard solution prepared by dissolving a mass of the substance equal to 2.719 g of pure sulfamic acid (equivalent mass: 97.09 g eq⁻¹) in water. To complete the neutralization of the resulting solution, further titration from the phenolphthalein to the methyl orange end point requires 0.0115 eq of HCl. Assuming each formula unit of NaOH completely dissociates in water to yield 2 ions, calculate the total number of ions furnished by NaOH in the initial mixture. (Take N_A = 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹). Give the answer to 3 significant figures.
